author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty view of the veterinarian directory lists every specialty the clinic knows, each with the veterinarians holding it, on one page reachable by its own address alone.
acceptance_criteria: The specialty directory answers at GET /specialties.html and no page of the system links to it.
Every specialty the clinic knows is listed under its stored name, all on one page, with no pagination.
Each veterinarian under a specialty is shown by first name followed by last name, for example "Helen Leary".
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it.
When the clinic knows no specialty at all, the page opens empty rather than failing.
The specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable order across repeated requests.
Two veterinarians sharing a full name are each listed under every specialty they hold.
The page adds no way to create, change, or remove a veterinarian or a specialty.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application - NG-2 is unchanged by this slice.
A navigation entry for the specialty directory, or a link to it from any other page. A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request.
Searching or filtering specialties - NG-9 stands.
notes: Address fixed by the product owner: GET /specialties.html. Kept out of docs/prd.md as mechanism; record it in system-design.md#contracts. REQ-LANG-002 binds the new page text: every new wording key must exist in all supported languages, none hard-coded. REQ-SYS-001 binds the page to carry the usual navigation, though nothing navigates to it. Three residual product questions are recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions and were not escalated, per the dispatch: entry ordering (only stability is required), whether an unheld specialty should be marked as held by none (it is listed with nothing under it), and whether a visible entry point follows. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is a second read-only page inside the existing vet feature package, built from patterns already in force: a Spring Data repository over a lookup entity (the PetTypeRepository shape), a package-private web controller, and a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets rendered through the shared layout fragment. The one adjustment is that no read path reaches specialties independently of veterinarians today, so a SpecialtyRepository is added; the grouping that pairs each specialty with its holders lands in an immutable SpecialtyDirectory value object rather than in the controller, because architecture-principles.md forbids extending the controller-held-rule deviation. system-design.md Contracts now carries the three new types and the route.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is served by a new package-private SpecialtyController in the vet package; VetController and its two routes are unchanged.

SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> (not JpaRepository) and exposes one read returning specialties in stored-name order; no write method is inherited, so NG-2 stays closed by the type's surface.
VetRepository.findAll() supplies the holders and is reused unchanged; it stays @Cacheable("vets"), and no new cache is declared in CacheConfiguration.
SpecialtyDirectory is constructed from the specialty list plus the vet collection and is the sole model attribute the template reads.
templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through fragments/layout with a menu key that matches no navigation item, so the page carries the usual navigation (REQ-SYS-001) while highlighting nothing.

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository returning every row in name order - the shape SpecialtyRepository follows
package-local repository extending Repository<T, Integer> rather than JpaRepository, keeping the exposed surface read-only
template registered against fragments/layout, heading and column labels driven by message keys; specialtyList.html mirrors it minus the pagination block
Value object (in force) covers SpecialtyDirectory; Web controller row bars the grouping from living in the controller

risks.risk: BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, and vets arrive from the "vets" cache while specialties arrive from a fresh query, so the two sources carry distinct Specialty instances for the same row.
risks.mitigation: Group holders by Specialty.getId(), never by object identity, Set membership, or name.

risks.risk: The specialties table indexes name without a uniqueness constraint on any vendor, so two specialties may share a stored name and grouping by name would merge them.
risks.mitigation: Key on identity and render the stored name; two same-named specialties list as two entries.

risks.risk: Ordering by name alone is not deterministic when names tie, which breaks the stable-order criterion and the two-veterinarians-sharing-a-full-name criterion.
risks.mitigation: Sort entries by specialty name then id, and holders by last name, first name, then id; never de-duplicate holder names.

risks.risk: A new message key that reaches only some bundles fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest, and any literal text in the template fails its hard-coded-string check.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys specialties, vets, name, and none; a genuinely new key goes into messages.properties and every locale bundle in the same commit.

risks.risk: The page inherits the vet cache's staleness, which has no eviction configured (system-design.md Open Questions item 5).
risks.mitigation: Accepted unchanged - the directory is exactly as stale as /vets.html; this slice adds no cache and no eviction.

notes: Placement deviates from the prd-entry file_targets on two paths, deliberately. (1) A new SpecialtyController rather than a third route on VetController: the naming rule wants a controller prefixed by the surface it serves, VetController's collaborator stays a single repository, and VetControllerTests needs no new @MockitoBean. (2) VetRepository is read, not edited - a Specialty query on a Repository<Vet, Integer> would need an explicit @Query returning a foreign type and would sit under the "vets" cache name. The prd-entry's test_names carry over verbatim to SpecialtyControllerTests. Narrowest readings taken where product input was open, per the dispatch: the mapping declares no @RequestParam at all (no page, no filter), so the only trust boundary the slice crosses has nothing to validate; an unheld specialty renders its name with nothing beneath it rather than a "held by none" marker; the empty-directory case renders the page with no entries. SpecialtyDirectory carries rendered display names as strings rather than Vet instances, which keeps the grouping unit-testable without Spring and keeps entities out of the view model. Vocabulary: "Specialty" and "Veterinarian" per docs/ubiquitous-language.md; "specialty directory" is the PRD's own phrase, so no new term is introduced. No ADR: every type matches an in-force catalog pattern and no alternative was rejected on a trade-off. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain note for a human or CI, not a defect in this change: no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in build.gradle, so no NVD match ran during this review and the framework versions were not verified against known CVEs. The change adds no dependency, so the un-run check is not implicated by this slice - recording it so the gap is not mistaken for a clean result.

The page performs an unpaged full read of every specialty plus every veterinarian on each request, and rebuilds the directory per request. VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets") so the vet read is served from cache, and the pre-existing /vets route already returns every veterinarian unpaged - the baseline is not made worse, and the row count is clinic-controlled rather than attacker-controlled. Worth remembering only if the specialty table ever becomes caller-influenced.
approved_aspects: No request-derived input reaches the new surface: GET /specialties.html declares no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, or request-bound command object, so the injection, mass-assignment, path-traversal, and cross-request-state rows of docs/security-principles.md are not implicated. No @InitBinder is needed because nothing binds.

Data access is a single static JPQL string in SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() with no parameters and no concatenation - no SQL/JPQL injection surface. It extends Repository rather than CrudRepository, so the read-only page inherits no write method: least privilege realized by construction, and stronger than the neighbouring VetRepository is obliged to be.
@Transactional(readOnly = true) matches the VetRepository pattern for the same concern, so the transaction posture does not diverge.

XSS: templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (entry.specialtyName, the veterinarian display names). No th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no remote script/link/img, no data:/javascript: href. The file mirrors vets/vetList.html line for line, so the escaping concern is secured the same way as its neighbour.

No request-derived text enters Thymeleaf preprocessing. The layout fragment's __${link}__ expression in fragments/layout.html is reached only with literal fragment arguments; the new template passes the literal 'specialties' as the menu name and no link, so it adds no expression-evaluation surface.

Exposed-surface row: the change adds one read-only GET returning specialty names and vet display names, which /vets.html and /vets already publish to the same anonymous callers. No new data class is exposed, no management endpoint exposure is broadened, and docs/system-design.md records the route, its absent request parameter, and its unpaged shape.

No secrets: the diff adds no credential, connection string, URL, or token, and no logging of any kind (no SLF4J call, no System.out/System.err). No exception message is constructed, so nothing new can reach the error page.

No shell execution, file I/O, XML/JSON/YAML parsing, reflection, regex, or randomness anywhere in the added production code - the corresponding checklist sections have no surface to review. SpecialtyDirectory is a plain model attribute with no Jackson or JAXB annotation, so it is not reachable from the content-negotiated /vets representation.

Thread safety: SpecialtyController holds only two repository references and no mutable state, so the singleton bean is safe under concurrent requests. SpecialtyDirectory and its Entry are records whose compact constructors defensively List.copyOf both lists, and the grouping HashMap in holdersBySpecialtyId is method-local and never escapes.
Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set, so the resolved dependency set is unchanged by this slice and no new artifact is introduced.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: No test anywhere executes the real JPQL query behind SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() ("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name") against a real database. SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a pure unit test against in-memory Specialty/Vet objects, and SpecialtyControllerTests substitutes a hand-written StoredSpecialties stand-in for the repository - both correctly avoid mocking internals, but the consequence is that the query string itself, and its mapping onto the seeded specialties table (src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql: radiology, surgery, dentistry), is never exercised. The codebase's own precedent for this tier exists: ClinicServiceTests is a @DataJpaTest that runs VetRepository.findAll() and PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes() against the same seeded H2 data (see shouldFindVets() at line 207) - SpecialtyRepository has no equivalent. A typo in the JPQL or a property-name mismatch would pass every current test and only surface at runtime.
findings.fix: Add a test method to ClinicServiceTests (mirroring shouldFindVets()) that autowires SpecialtyRepository and asserts findSpecialties() returns the three seeded specialties (dentistry, radiology, surgery) in name order, exercising the real @Query against the H2 test database.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a clean, framework-free unit suite (9 tests, 100% instruction/branch coverage on SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyDirectory.Entry per jacocoTestReport) that directly covers every design-block risk: grouping by Specialty.getId() rather than object identity or Set membership (theDirectoryShouldMatchHoldersOnSpecialtyIdentityRatherThanInstance), two specialties sharing a stored name staying apart (theDirectoryShouldKeepTwoSpecialtiesSharingAStoredNameApart), and the full tie-break ordering on both entries and holders

SpecialtyControllerTests's hand-written StoredSpecialties/EmployedVeterinarians stand-ins are the brief's preferred choice for new tests (testing-principles.md Mocking Policy: 'a new test reaches for a real implementation or a hand-written double first'), not a deviation from VetControllerTests's @MockitoBean usage - correctly diverges from the neighboring file because the brief's rule is prospective, not retroactive
All six controller tests carry the prd-entry test names verbatim and their bodies match those names' claims one-to-one, including the empty-directory and no-pagination-link acceptance criteria
Four-phase structure held throughout, no phase comments or narration, fluent AssertJ exclusively, no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue

Three-tier data naming is respected: SOME_SPECIALTY names the one truly irrelevant specialty value, all other literals (radiology/surgery/dentistry, Helen/Leary, ids) are meaningful to their assertion and expected values are derived from the same inputs the test constructs (self-verifying), construction is fully behind factory methods (createASpecialty/createAVeterinarian/createVeterinarian/anEntry)
100% jacoco coverage on SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyDirectory.Entry, and SpecialtyController; ./gradlew test green for the full suite including the new 15 tests

author: change-grader
summary: add the read-only specialty directory page

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module, no sensitive paths, and almost entirely additive: three new classes, one new template, two new test classes. The only edits to existing code are two docs files and one added test method, so no existing route or production file changes behavior, and the new page is reachable only by its own address.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks against the surrounding code turned up nothing the diff would not lead you to expect. Holders are grouped by specialty id rather than object identity or name, which is the right key given the entities carry no equals; unheld specialties fall back to an empty list; Vet.specialties is eagerly fetched so the detached cached vets render safely; the repository extends the bare Repository interface so no write method is inherited; every dynamic value in the template goes through escaping th:text, and all three message keys it uses already exist. The one judgment call is that holders sort by last name while they display first name first, so the visible order can look unsorted; it is deliberate, commented, tested, and the requirement asks only for a stable order.

test_adequacy.note: Fifteen tests across three tiers that exercise real behavior rather than restate it: nine framework-free unit tests on the grouping, six that render the actual template through MockMvc against hand-written repository stand-ins and assert on page content including what must not appear, and one database test whose expected order differs from the seed insertion order, so it cannot pass unless the query's ordering clause really runs. Every boundary the requirement names is covered. The one untested claim is that no other page links to the new address; I confirmed by search that nothing references it today, but no test guards that from regressing.

reviewer_hedging.note: The roster approved unanimously, but not silently. The test reviewer requested changes in round one over an untested database query, which the implementer fixed and the reviewer then approved. More to the point, the security reviewer attached recommendations to both approvals, including the final one: dependency CVE scanning is not configured in this build, so no vulnerability check ran during review, and the reviewer names an external CI or human check as the closing step. It also parked a performance note that the page reads every specialty and every veterinarian unpaged on each request. Neither is a defect in this change, and both are pre-existing project conditions, but they are residuals the pipeline deliberately hands to you rather than resolves.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions and no consultations, and the single build retry was a planned progress checkpoint rather than a broken build. The implemented paths match the design decision exactly, and the change adds no navigation entry, no write path, and nothing beyond the stated surface.

rationale: The code itself is clean and the tests are real, so this reads fast. The reason to pause is what the reviewers parked rather than fixed: no dependency vulnerability scan runs in this build, which the security reviewer flags as needing an external check. Confirm you accept that standing gap, then merge.
